options.label: Fatebound (Level 1)
options.description:
Least Milestone Feature

When you achieve the first milestone of this thread, you gain your choice of one the following benefits.

Dream Gift. A god, Norn, or other powerful being has given you a gift in a dream. When you awoke, you had a Common magic item of the GM’s choice that may aid you.

Fate’s Blessing. Once per day, while you are Bloodied, you can use your Reaction to get Advantage on a saving throw.

Your fate is written. Make it glorious.

Many warriors loudly boast of their desire for a noble death or an honorable end in battle, to thus earn a seat in the great hall of Valhalla. These boasts are but hopeful wishes since most individuals never see the path of their future. You, however, are not most individuals. You have been blessed, or perhaps cursed, with the knowledge of your end, though this knowledge doesn’t tell you if you succeed or fail in the circumstance surrounding your death. You might know you will die facing a dark warlord, but you don’t know if you will defeat her. Despite this, the Norns have given you a rare opportunity. The knowledge you possess will help you ensure your death is worthy of the sagas.

Some of those who are Fatebound are marked from birth. Others learn of their fate from seers, shamans, or divine visions. Some heroes earn this thread after engaging in activities that move the gods or the Norns to reward them with such a potent end.

Fatebound and Death. Keep in mind that having this thread may mean you can’t die before your fated time, but it doesn’t mean you will reach that point whole and healthy. While your fate is inevitable, luck alone determines your condition when you meet that end. Do you lead a glorious charge across the battlefield? Or are you left guarding the baggage? Has every confrontation leading up to your end prepared you to defeat your ultimate foe? Or has a lifetime of avoidance left you ill-prepared?

If a Fatebound PC is killed before their time, and magical resurrection is not an option, a GM could instead choose for them to be injured in a significant way—such as the loss of a limb or eye. These injuries should not be able to be healed without high-level magic. Alternatively, perhaps they lose one of their powerful magical items instead of their lives, or they might suffer a level of Exhaustion until they reach their next milestone. The GM and player should agree on this complication.

Goals. Work with your GM to create a goal specific to your campaign or use one from the Fatebound Goals table. The specific nature of each milestone is dependent on the goal selected and should be agreed upon by both player and GM. Use the suggested milestone benefits described in this section or create new ones based on the rules for creating a thread.

GM Note: The Fatebound is an unusual thread in that its final milestone specifically describes the manner in which a character might meet with a permanent death, likely as part of the final accomplishment of their goal, and then empowers the PCs’ allies as a reward. Most importantly, this thread should be something the player consciously selects.

Fatebound Goals
d6 Goal
1 I will die only after finding and facing the mightiest dragon in the land.
2 I will be slain by Utgard-Loki while attempting to thwart his plan to slay the gods.
3 To defend my people from invasion, I pledge to pay any price, including my own life.
4 I shall search for and find a fabled lost treasure, but I will die in the process.
5 I will rise to become the North’s greatest reaver, then perish battling the World Serpent.
6 I seek the truth behind the fall of Nordheim, though it will cost my life to learn it.

options.description:

Enduring Wyrd. When you take damage, you may use your Reaction to gain Temporary Hit Points equal to your Proficiency Bonus. You cannot use this feature again until you complete a Short or Long Rest.

options.description:

Last Act of Fate. At a moment you have predetermined to be the time when you are to die, when you are reduced 0 Hit Points or killed outright, you may (no action required) instead set your Hit Points to 1. You lose any detrimental conditions, and any harmful effects on you are ended immediately. Until the end of your next turn, you gain Advantage on all attack rolls and ability checks, you have Immunity to all damage and conditions (and other effects at the GM’s discretion), and you add your character level to all damage rolls.

At the end of your next turn, you die and can never be restored to life.

Glorious End. If you achieve your destiny in a way that earns you a seat in Valhalla (or some other appropriate afterlife), the allies who witness your death have Advantage on all d20 rolls for 24 hours as they are inspired by your heroism.

options.label: Herald (Level 1)
options.description:
Least Milestone Feature

When you achieve the first milestone of this thread, you gain the following benefits.

Storyteller’s Knack. You learn three languages of your choice.

Performer’s Reward. If you have at least 3 days of downtime between adventures, you can earn GP equal to 10 times your character level by performing your stories in taverns, on the street, or for powerful patrons. Additional downtime events don’t increase this reward.

Your stories don’t just recount events . . . they shape history.

Storytellers are revered in the Northlands. Whether a skald sharing tales around a fire, a lore keeper gathering sagas to pass down the generations, or a grizzled reaver frightening young warriors by recalling harrowing battles, the tradition of collecting stories is respected across nearly all cultures in the region. As a Herald, you are a proud, if temporary, part of this tradition, driven by a need to spread stories during your travels to accomplish a specific end.

Perhaps your stories encourage downtrodden karls to rise up against their cruel jarl, warn a region about an approaching invasion, or convince warriors to join your cause. Part skald, part herald, part envoy, you will use your tales and stories to sway the minds of your audience and help shape the world.

Goals. Work with your GM to create a goal specific to your campaign or use one from the Herald Goals table. The specific nature of each milestone is dependent on the goal selected and should be agreed upon by both player and GM. Use the suggested milestone benefits described in this section or create new ones based on the rules for creating a thread.

GM Note. This thread brings flavorful Northlands themes into a campaign and can be taken up by characters of any class. However, it can tread on the toes of any Bards in the party. Consult with your Bard players before allowing a character to take on this thread to make sure no feelings will be hurt.

Herald Goals
d6 Goal
1 The feared invasion from Jotunheim approaches, and the country must be warned.
2 By telling the sagas, I will gather support for the greatest raid the North has ever launched.
3 My tales flatter Thor and Wotan in the hope they will support our struggle against the forces of Chernobog and Angrboda.
4 I spread the word of the great crusade to eradicate the darkness beneath Tanserhall. Heed my call!
5 I seek a lost treasure of Hyperborea, and by spreading tales of similar treasures, I hope to find a path to a hidden vault.
6 To rouse the people against their evil king, I shall assemble an array of sorrowful tales of corruption that cannot be ignored.

options.label: Herald (Level 5)
options.description:

Use Charisma as your spellcasting ability score. After casting one of these spells using this feature, you can’t use the feature again until you finish a Long Rest.

After you spend at least 10 minutes telling an inspiring story or legend, choose either one creature who can hear you, or up to three creatures. You can’t select yourself as a target. Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until for 7 days.

Depending on the number of targets, creatures can receive one of the following.

Luck Boon (Three Targets). Once before the next Long Rest, a target can expend their boon to gain Advantage on a saving throw, attack roll, or ability check.

Wyrd Boon (One Target). Once before their next Long Rest, if the target does not succeed on a saving throw or attack roll, they can choose to succeed instead. An attack roll succeeding in this way results in the minimum needed to succeed (not a Critical Hit, for example).

Song of Matrimony. A member of the royal family in a particular land has fallen in love with you and your performances, and the feeling is mutual. You are engaged to marry into the royal family.

options.label: Legend Hunter (Level 1)
options.description:
Least Milestone Feature

When you achieve the first milestone of this thread, you gain the following benefit.

Predator’s Mark. You have Advantage on Wisdom (Survival) checks made to track creatures, and on a failed check it only takes you half the time to reacquire the tracks (5 minutes in a confined area, or half an hour outdoors).

Neither storm nor night nor bloody fang shall slow your relentless pursuit.

Hunting is as old as the Northlands itself. From volcanic peaks to frigid fens and aurora-bathed glaciers, the tales of hunters are sung alongside those of heroes and gods. While some may hunt for survival or vengeance, you are different. You are a hunter to be feared, as you hunt for the thrill of the chase and the glory of victory.

As a Legend Hunter, you may have been chosen by the Norns, blessed by a god, or forged in trials of blood and grift. No matter how you come to it, your extraordinary search for greater and greater prey sets you apart from those who hunt merely for survival. You do not merely forge trails; you craft sagas. You do not merely slay beasts; you end legends to become a legend.

Goals. Work with your GM to create a goal specific to your campaign or use one from the Legend Hunter Goals table. The specific nature of each milestone is dependent on the goal selected and should be agreed upon by both player and GM. Use the suggested milestone benefits described in this section or create new ones based on the rules for creating a thread.

Legend Hunter Goals
d6 Goal
1 I will prove my valor by tracking down and slaying a legendary monster that has been destroying villages.
2 I hunt for a mythical two-headed jotun somewhere in the Bleak Expanse.
3 Besting a great dragon in its lair shall be my ultimate victory.
4 I will go beneath the waves to bring low the mother of all krakens.
5 I will bring back the head of Fenris.
6 My legend will be assured when I go among the roots of Yggdrasil to slay Nidhogg.

options.label: Legend Hunter (Level 5)
options.description:
Lesser Milestone Feature

Unclouded Sight. Your honed senses let you ignore obscurement caused by weather, such as rain, snow, or fog. This includes magical clouds and weather effects, such as Fog Cloud and Sleet Storm, but not Darkness.

Reliable Senses. After failing an Intelligence (Investigation), Wisdom (Perception), or Wisdom (Survival) check, you can reroll the check and take the higher result. Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

options.description:

When you achieve this level of milestone, you gain the following benefit.

Legend Breaker. When you hit a creature that has Legendary Resistance or Legendary Actions, you can choose to forgo dealing damage to force that creature to make a Constitution saving throw (DC 8 plus your Strength or Wisdom modifier and your Proficiency Bonus). On a failed save, the target becomes unable use its Legendary Resistance or its Legendary Actions. The target can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success. Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

The Ultimate Favor. You performed a service for a powerful healer, who was caught in an animal trap set by another hunter. In return, they have offered to cast a single spell of healing of 6th to 9th level on you or a creature of your choice, at a time of your choosing, even if this puts them at great risk. This should be a spell that heals, regenerates, resurrects, or that removes conditions or curses.

options.label: Sworn Huskarl (Level 1)
options.description:
Least Milestone Feature

When you achieve the first milestone of this thread, you gain the following benefit.

Jarl’s Authority. The authority granted you by your loyal service can sway the opinions of others. Before rolling an Intimidation or Persuasion check to influence someone who knows and respects (or fears) your ruler, you can choose to treat the d20 roll as if you’d rolled a natural 15. Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

You carry out the will of your king, no matter the risk.

You have pledged your loyalty to an important personage, promising to guard them or travel across the Northlands in their service, risking danger as you seek to accomplish a great task. In the past, it was expected that a huskarl would swear to serve a lord for life or until they were dismissed. While jarls still take huskarls in that way, they also accept the service of huskarls on a temporary basis, to perform specific deeds or until certain threats are dealt with. These are the types of huskarls described in this thread.

The sworn huskarl enjoys a position of respect within their lord’s retinue. More than a mere bodyguard, you are a trusted agent acting on your ruler’s behalf. You carry some of their authority with you, but that also comes with the responsibility to act in ways they would approve. Sworn huskarls who bring shame to their jarl don’t remain in service for long.

A jarl takes on a new huskarl with a simple ceremony in which the huskarl swears an oath in the longhouse before a gathering of other members of the felag. During the oath-swearing, the goals or timeframe for the service are mentioned (unless the jarl keeps your mission a secret). Traditionally, your reasons for serving are respect for the lord, payment, or power. However, in some cases your oath may hold a secret. Perhaps you made it under threat of violence or under false pretenses. Or maybe your lord doesn’t deserve such loyalty. You might serve under protest or with your own goal that’s unknown to your ruler.

Goals. Work with your GM to create a goal specific to your campaign or use one from the Sworn Huskarl Goals table. The specific nature of each milestone is dependent on the goal selected and should be agreed upon by both player and GM. Use the suggested milestone benefits described in this section or create new ones based on the rules for creating a thread.

Sworn Huskarl Goals
d6 Goal
1 I will find my king’s long-lost child so that my kingdom will have a true heir.
2 My queen depends on me to find and slay the pretender who claims a blood right to her throne.
3 I must root out a hidden sect of the Cult of Ragnarok that grows within my jarl’s land.
4 Giant raiding parties threaten the land. My jarl calls upon me to destroy them and make the land safe once more.
5 I can only earn my freedom by finding the stolen crown of my sadistic monarch.
6 I serve only until I can discover a way to overthrow this corrupt king, who took the throne through dark sorcery.

Jarl’s Gift. To help you carry out their will, your ruler gives you your choice of one of the following uncommon magic items (or another you and your GM agree upon): Bracers of Archery, Defender’s Honey, Sentinel Shield, +1 Wand of the War Mage, or +1 Weapon.

options.label: Alliance
options.description:
Your faction is the Alliance.

The peoples of the Alliance are bound together by proud traditions of nobility, honor, faith, justice, and sacrifice. The disparate cultures that make up this faction contribute technical, arcane, and spiritual wisdom toward the goal of a peaceful and just world. The highest ideals of the Alliance are tradition, justice, and duty, matching closely to the Lawful Good alignment.

The Alliance is a military coalition whose leadership is dependent on the unified will of its member peoples. By default, the high king (or other leader) of Stormwind has served as commander of the Alliance, but the commander has authority over only the military forces that other Alliance leaders commit to the Alliance’s cause. Thus, in practice, the human king leads as part of a council made up of all the Alliance leaders.

options.label: Horde
options.description:
Your faction is the Horde.

The proud nations of the Horde are loosely joined in an alliance of convenience against a hostile world that would see them destroyed. Focused and ferocious, the Horde values strength and honor but struggles to keep its members’ aggression in check. The Horde’s ideals are unity, freedom, and hope, matching closely to the Chaotic Good alignment.

From the time of its founding until the end of the Fourth War, the Horde was led by a single warchief. The orc shaman Thrall held that position from before the Third War until he stepped down to join the Earthen Ring (described later in this chapter) during the Cataclysm. He was succeeded by the warmongering Garrosh Hellscream, who was in turn deposed by a combination of Alliance pressure and a rebellion of the Darkspear trolls. The troll chieftain Vol’jin then took up the mantle, becoming the first non-orc to hold the title, but Vol’jin died during the Burning Legion’s third invasion of Azeroth. The undead high elf Sylvanas Windrunner then became warchief, but she ultimately abandoned the Horde to pursue her own agenda. Since her departure, a Horde Council made up of the leaders of the Horde’s subfactions has governed the Horde.

The knightly Order of the Argent Dawn is dedicated to protecting Azeroth from the Burning Legion, the Scourge, and other forces that seek to destroy the world. Neutral in the continual conflict between the Alliance and the Horde (and generally Neutral Good in alignment), the Argent Dawn calls both factions allies in its higher purpose of resisting these forces of evil. The order’s headquarters is Light’s Hope Chapel, in the Eastern Plaguelands—a beacon of hope and comfort in a barren and twisted land—and the knights operate across the Plaguelands and anywhere evil rears its head.

In addition to pursuing quests assigned to them by the Argent Dawn, characters can increase their Renown Score by killing powerful Fiends and Undead and bringing evidence of the monsters’ destruction to Argent Dawn agents.

Named for Cenarius—the demigod who trained Malfurion Stormrage, the first druid—the Cenarion Circle is a worldwide order keeping watch over Azeroth’s druids and protecting the natural balance. Since the end of the Third War, the circle has accepted druids from both the Alliance and the Horde, reflecting a generally Neutral alignment. In the druidic sanctuary of Moonglade, night elf and tauren druids live and work in harmony, and in recent years, druids from other peoples—Kul Tiran humans, worgen, trolls, and even haranir—have joined the ranks of the Cenarion Circle. The order is still led by Cenarius himself, with the involvement of Malfurion and the tauren druid Hamuul Runetotem.

The Cenarion Circle is most active in Kalimdor. Besides Moonglade, which is inaccessible to anyone but circle members, the order also has a base in Desolace (Karnum’s Glade). It has launched expeditions into Silithus, the Plaguelands, and Outland, and its members are on the forefront of any effort to preserve, protect, or restore nature.

The Earthen Ring is a gathering of Azeroth’s most powerful shaman, working together to preserve the balance among the elements. The members of the Earthen Ring oppose destructive forces such as the Twilight’s Hammer cult, the rampaging black dragon Deathwing, and the Burning Legion, and they work tirelessly to heal the wounds inflicted on Azeroth by such forces. Insisting on a neutral stance in mortal conflicts (and a generally Neutral alignment), the Earthen Ring welcomes members from both the Alliance and the Horde, though the peoples of the Alliance— particularly draenei, Wildhammer dwarves, and humans of Kul Tiras—are recent additions to the organization. It also includes murlocs, the Krokul draenei, and other druids who haven’t chosen a side in the Alliance–Horde conflict.

The Earthen Ring is governed by the Elder Council, which gathers at a shrine perched at the edge of the Maelstrom called the Heart of Azeroth. The order also maintains a ritual circle just outside Stormwind’s walls (the Eastern Earthshrine) and another above Orgrimmar (the Western Earthshrine). Both circles include portals leading to the Elemental Plane and other areas of Earthen Ring activity, which Earthen Ring shaman allow only those who are at least Honored with the faction to use.

Training

Several renown perks give you the opportunity to work with a trainer to learn a language or gain a proficiency. The days required needn’t be consecutive, but you must spend 8 consecutive hours with the trainer for a day to count. You can gain only one tool proficiency from each renown perk.

Affiliated with the Alliance and the Horde respectively, the Explorers’ League and the Reliquary are scholarly organizations dedicated to the practice of archaeology and the study of history, seeking to understand the origins of life and culture on Azeroth.

Magni Bronzebeard, the king of Ironforge, founded the Explorers’ League by decree after dwarf-led expeditions uncovered surprising facts about the dwarves’ connection to the ancient titans. Declaring that learning this history was more important than mining and engineering, Magni directed the Explorers’ League to focus on archaeological work and plumbing the secrets of the ancient world. The league quickly expanded its scope to encompass natural history as well as the history of all Azeroth’s peoples, and it soon accepted citizens of other Alliance nations as members. High Explorer Muninn Magellas is the leader of the Explorers’ League, and the organization’s headquarters remains in Ironforge, in the Hall of Explorers.

The Reliquary, in contrast, began as an effort to harness the power of ancient relics for the benefit of the blood elves and their allies in the Horde. The leader and founder of the Reliquary, Tae’thelan Bloodwatcher, believed such artifacts should be carefully studied, not feared. Tae’thelan’s ultimate goal in founding the Reliquary was to free the blood elves from their magical addiction and reunite them. When the blood elves joined the Horde, the Reliquary opened its membership to all members of the Horde, but its headquarters (also called the Reliquary) remains in Silvermoon City.

Relic Rivals

Despite their different origins (and different alignments, corresponding to the difference between the Alliance and the Horde), the Explorers’ League and the Reliquary use similar methods and often vie for access to the same sites. For most of recent history, the organizations were bitter rivals, with the tension between them often erupting into violent conflict. During this time, the factions are mutually hostile (see “Mutually Hostile Factions”).

However, with the reemergence of the Dragon Isles and the subsequent discovery of Khaz Algar, the two organizations have set aside their old rivalry and formed joint expeditions. During this period, a character’s Renown Score with either faction applies to both factions, so having a Renown Score of 3+ with either one makes members of both factions Friendly by default.

Mutually Hostile Factions

World of Warcraft features many opposing factions that are so hostile to each other that any renown gain with one faction automatically results in a loss of renown with the other. The Explorers’ League and the Reliquary were mutually hostile before they were forced to cooperate in exploring the Dragon Isles. Other examples include the Scryers and the Aldor of Shattrath City, as well as the Frenzyheart Tribe of wolvar and the gorlock Oracles of Sholazar Basin. In situations like these, a character’s Renown Score with a faction can drop below 0, which means members of that faction are Hostile to the character by default.

Charm of Pandaria. While you have this Charm, you know the Pandaren language. You can expend the Charm to cast Gaseous Form, targeting yourself. The effect lasts for 1 hour or until you end the effect as a Bonus Action.
Charm of the Burning Legion. While you have this Charm, you know the Eredun language. You can expend the Charm to cast Rain of Fire (level 4 version).
Charm of the Highborne. While you have this Charm, you know Thalassian. You can expend the Charm to cast Charm Monster.
Charm of the Old Gods. While you have this Charm, you know Shath’Yar. You can expend the Charm to cast Summon Aberration.
Charm of the Titan-Forged. While you have this Charm, you know Titan. You can expend the Charm to gain Resistance to all damage for 1 minute as your flesh takes on a mineral appearance.
Charm of the Zandalari. While you have this Charm, you know Zandali. You can expend the Charm to cast Summon Beast (level 4 version). The summoned Bestial Spirit resembles a loa.

options.description:
Prerequisite: Renown 3+ with the Kirin Tor

You can enjoy a Modest lifestyle in Dalaran at no cost. You can also request a favor from the archmages of the Kirin Tor, which can take one of the following forms:

  • An archmage casts for you a spell of level 3 or lower at half the usual cost.
  • An archmage provides you with a Common or Uncommon magic item from the Arcana tables in the Dungeon Master’s Guide at half the usual cost.
  • An archmage spends 30 days teaching you, so you learn a language from the tables in chapter 2 or gain proficiency with a tool (see “Training”).

You can request such a favor a number of times equal to your Renown Score with the Kirin Tor. If your Renown Score falls below the number of favors you have requested, a higher-ranking member of the Kirin Tor might call in a favor from you, sending you on a mission for the organization.

Other members of the faction are Friendly to you by default.

Training

Several renown perks give you the opportunity to work with a trainer to learn a language or gain a proficiency. The days required needn’t be consecutive, but you must spend 8 consecutive hours with the trainer for a day to count. You can gain only one tool proficiency from each renown perk.

The Kirin Tor began as a secretive mages’ guild within the Empire of Arathor, the first great human civilization of the Eastern Kingdoms. Viewed with suspicion by much of the populace, the mages of Arathor secluded themselves in their own city, Dalaran, which became a beacon to mages from across Azeroth. With the fall of Arathor, Dalaran became a nation in its own right, one of Arathor’s seven successor kingdoms, and the Council of Six who led the Kirin Tor became the rulers of this city-state. Razed during the Third War, Dalaran was rebuilt behind powerful warding spells and later transformed into a flying island that could be relocated to safety when needed. From its original site in the Hillsbrad Foothills, Dalaran moved first to Northrend’s Crystalsong Forest, then above Karazhan in Deadwind Pass, then to the Broken Isles, then above the Isle of Dorn in Khaz Algar. There it met its doom at the hands of Xal’atath’s forces of the Void, but the survivors of the Kirin Tor remain in Dornogal, coordinating the magical defense of Azeroth.

The Council of Six, the leadership of the Kirin Tor, is made up of the most senior members of the Kirin Tor. Its leaders have included Archmage Rhonin, who oversaw the rebuilding of Dalaran after the Third War, Lady Jaina Proudmoore, and Archmage Khadgar, who was imprisoned by Xal’atath just before Dalaran’s destruction. The Kirin Tor is generally Lawful Neutral in alignment.

In addition, when you request a favor from the Kirin Tor, it can take one of the following additional forms:

  • An archmage casts for you a spell of level 4 or lower at half the usual cost.
  • An archmage provides you with a magic item of Rare rarity of lower from the Arcana tables in the Dungeon Master’s Guide at half the usual cost.
  • Whenever you take a Bastion turn, you can issue the Research order to the Kirin Tor as if it were a Library facility in your Bastion.

The Steamwheedle Cartel is one of the largest and richest goblin cartels, having maintained a careful neutrality in the conflict between the Alliance and the Horde since the Second War (and a generally Neutral alignment). From its headquarters in Gadgetzan (in Tanaris), the cartel oversees operations across Azeroth and even Outland. It also runs Booty Bay (in Stranglethorn), Ratchet (in the Northern Barrens), and Everlook (in Winterspring), as well as smaller outposts. The cartel’s hands are in virtually every line of work, with a specialty in premium- grade alchemy (at least since the alchemist Marin Noggenfogger assumed the position of trade prince). Besides potions, the cartel also deals in fuels, poisons, and industrial chemicals—what some goblins describe as “liquid assets.”

The Valdrakken Accord is the unified might of all dragonkind, seeking to protect not only the Dragon Isles but all of Azeroth according to the ancient charge given to the five Dragon Aspects (see chapter 6). The accord has also expanded its mission to include dragons beyond the five flights—in particular those who follow Vyranoth, who has been empowered as the Aspect of Storms.

The mission of the Dragon Aspects means that what is good for dragonkind is generally beneficial for all of Azeroth. The dragons oppose the Burning Legion, the lingering forces of the Old Gods and elementals they have corrupted, the remnants of the Scourge, the powers of the Void, and any other force that might threaten Azeroth and its inhabitants. That said, working with the dragons means viewing the world’s conflicts from their perspective (which is generally Neutral) and solving problems their way.

The leaders of the Valdrakken Accord are the six Dragon Aspects: Alexstrasza, Nozdormu, Kalecgos, Merithra, Ebyssian, and Vyranoth. Their base of operations is the city of Valdrakken in the Dragon Isles.

Before the Dragon Isles reappeared, the Wyrmrest Accord carried out a similar mission but without the black dragonflight.

options.label: Valdrakken Accord: Honored
options.description:
Valdrakken Accord: Honored

When you cast the spell in this way, your familiar is a crimson proto-whelp (Pseudodragon). Once you cast the spell in this way, you can’t do so again until you finish a Long Rest. You lose the Blessing and your proto-whelp familiar vanishes if your Renown Score with the Valdrakken Accord falls below 10.

Also, if you establish your Bastion in the Dragon Isles, it includes a Garden special facility. This facility doesn’t count toward the total number of special facilities in your Bastion. The hireling departs and the facility becomes unusable if your Renown Score with Valdrakken Accord falls below 10.

Prerequisite: Renown 10+ with Stormwind

When you use tailoring to craft an item (see chapter 3), the time required to craft it is halved.

You can purchase equipment found in the Player’s Handbook, as well as Common or Uncommon magic items, from merchants of the faction at a 10% discount.

options.label: Stormwind: Revered
options.description:

You can request a supernatural gift from the leaders of Stormwind before you undertake a quest on their behalf. You receive any Blessing or Charm from the Dungeon Master’s Guide, and it lasts until you complete or abandon the quest or expend it. Once you request this gift, you can’t do so again until your Renown Score with Stormwind increases.

Your faction discount increases to 15% and extends to Rare magic items.

Stormwind: Exalted

Prerequisite: Renown 50+ with Stormwind

You can call on Stormwind forces to assist you for a single adventure. You receive your choice of one of the following groups:

  • Fifty human soldiers (Warrior Infantry) led by three sergeants (Warrior Veterans) and one commander (Warrior Commander)
  • Three SI:7 agents (Scout Captains) and their leader (Spy Master)
  • A champion of the Holy Light (Questing Knight)
  • A Kul Tiran admiral (Pirate Admiral) with a [vehicle]Warship[/vehicle] (you must hire the ship’s crew)

Once you request this assistance, you can’t do so again until your Renown Score with Stormwind increases.

Your faction discount increases to 25% and extends to Very Rare magic items.

Bilgewater Cartel Renown Perks

The Bilgewater Cartel represents goblins aligned with the Horde. The cartel’s capital is Bilgewater Harbor in Azshara, and it has significant holdings across Azeroth. The cartel’s leader is Trade Prince Monte Gazlowe, who succeeded Jastor Gallywix in that role after Jastor abandoned the cartel. The cartel’s business has been described as “the classical goblin arts: building things and blowing them up.” Engineering, construction, infrastructure, and demolitions are all in the Bilgewater wheelhouse.

While your Bastion is in Bilgewater Harbor or any other Bilgewater holding, your Renown Score with the Bilgewater Cartel increases by 1.

This Charm allows you to cast the Summon Construct spell (Metal only), which lasts for 1 hour and doesn’t require Concentration. The Construct Spirit appears as a mechanical goblin. When it drops to 0 Hit Points or the spell ends, the summoned spirit explodes in a 10-foot-radius Sphere of fire. Creatures in the Sphere make a DC 13 Dexterity saving throw, taking 2d6 Fire damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one.

The Charm lasts until you use it once or you complete or abandon the quest. Once you request this Charm, you can’t do so again until your Renown Score with the Bilgewater Cartel increases.

Your faction discount increases to 15% and extends to Rare magic items.

Prerequisite: Renown 25+ with the Dark Talons

You can request a Charm from the leaders of the Dark Talons before you undertake a quest on their behalf. You receive the Charm of Terror, and it lasts until you use it three times or you complete or abandon the quest. You can take a Magic action to release a wave of terror. Each creature of your choice within 30 feet of you must succeed on a DC 15 Wisdom saving throw or have the Frightened condition for 1 minute. While Frightened, a creature must spend its turns trying to move as far away from you as it can, and it can’t make Opportunity Attacks. For its action, it can take only the Dash action or an action to try to escape from an effect that prevents it from moving. If it has nowhere it can move, the creature can take the Dodge action. At the end of each of its turns, a creature repeats the save, ending the effect on itself on a success.

Once you request this Charm, you can’t do so again until your Renown Score with the Dark Talons increases.

options.label: Darkspear Tribe: Honored
options.description:
Darkspear Tribe: Honored

Prerequisite: Renown 10+ with the Darkspear Tribe

During a Short Rest, you can make offerings to the loa revered by trolls to gain a Charm. When you finish the rest, make a DC 15 Intelligence (Religion) check. On a successful check, you gain a Charm that allows you to gain the benefit of one of the following Potions as a Bonus Action (choose when you gain the Charm): Potion of Animal Friendship, Potion of Climbing, Potion of Comprehension, Potion of Fire Breath, Potion of Giant Strength (hill), Potion of Growth, Potion of Healing (greater), Potion of Mana (greater), Potion of Pugilism, Potion of Resistance (your choice of damage type), or Potion of Water Breathing.

The Charm vanishes from you after you use it, if you use this feature again, or if your Renown Score with the Darkspear tribe falls below 10. Once you receive a Charm in this way, you can’t gain another until your Renown Score with the Darkspear tribe increases.

Silvermoon City: Honored

Prerequisite: Renown 10+ with Silvermoon City

When you use enchanting to craft an item (see chapter 3), the time required to craft it is halved.

 You can purchase equipment found in the Player’s Handbook, as well as Common or Uncommon magic items, from merchants of the faction at a 10% discount.

Silvermoon City: Friendly

Prerequisite: Renown 3+ with Silvermoon City

You can spend 30 days with a trainer to learn Shalassian or Thalassian or to gain proficiency with Carpenter’s Tools, Potter’s Tools, or Woodcarver’s Tools.

Other members of the faction are Friendly to you by default.

options.label: Silvermoon City: Revered
options.description:
Silvermoon City: Revered

Prerequisite: Renown 25+ with Silvermoon City

You can request a Charm from the leaders of Silvermoon City before you undertake a quest on their behalf. You receive a Charm that duplicates the effect of one of the following Wands: Wand of Binding, Wand of Enemy Detection, Wand of Fear, Wand of Fireballs, Wand of Lightning Bolts, Wand of Magic Missiles, Wand of Paralysis, Wand of Polymorph, or Wand of Web. The Charm doesn’t regain charges. It vanishes from you if you spend all its charges, if you complete or abandon the quest, or if your Renown Score with Silvermoon City falls below 25. Once you request a Charm, you can’t do so again until your Renown Score with Silvermoon City increases.

Your faction discount increases to 15% and extends to Rare magic items.

You can spend 30 days with a trainer to learn Taurahe or gain proficiency with the Herbalism Kit (see “Training”).

Other members of the faction are Friendly to you by default.

Training

Several renown perks give you the opportunity to work with a trainer to learn a language or gain a proficiency. The days required needn’t be consecutive, but you must spend 8 consecutive hours with the trainer for a day to count. You can gain only one tool proficiency from each renown perk.

Thunder Bluff Renown Perks

The Thunder Bluff faction represents those united tauren tribes who have aligned themselves with the Horde, including the Highmountain tauren of the Broken Isles and some taunka of Northrend. The leader of the faction is High Chieftain Baine Bloodhoof, who succeeded his father, Cairne Bloodhoof, when Cairne died in an ill-fated duel against Garrosh Hellscream.

While your Bastion is in Thunder Bluff or elsewhere in Mulgore or Highmountain, your Renown Score with Thunder Bluff increases by 1.

Undercity Renown Perks

The Undercity faction encompasses the Forsaken aligned with the Horde. The faction was long led by Sylvanas Windrunner, who originally led the Forsaken who broke free from the control of the Lich King. When Sylvanas stepped into the leadership of the Horde as warchief, the Desolate Council was formed to govern the Forsaken in her place. The council, based now in the Ruins of Lordaeron, is made up of five leaders: Calia Menethil, Lilian Voss, Master Apothecary Faranell, Deathstalker Commander Belmont, and Dark Ranger Velonara.

class.name: Hunter’s Mark
class.description:
You always have the Hunter’s Mark spell prepared. You can cast it twice without expending a spell slot, and you regain all expended uses of this ability when you finish a Long Rest.

The number of times you can cast the spell without a spell slot increases when you reach certain Ranger levels.
class.snippet: You always have Hunter’s Mark prepared and can cast it without expending a spell slot {{limiteduse}} times per Long Rest.

class.name: Hunter’s Lore
class.description: You can call on the forces of nature to reveal certain strengths and weaknesses of your prey. While a creature is marked by your [spells]Hunter’s Mark[/spells], you know whether that creature has any Immunities, Resistances, or Vulnerabilities, and if the creature has any, you know what they are.
class.snippet: When a creature is marked by your Hunter’s Mark, you know whether the creature has any Immunities, Resistances, Vulnerabilities, and if the creature has any, you know what they are.

class.name: Initiate a Circle Spell
class.description: You take a Magic action to initiate casting a Circle spell. When you do so, choose which Circle casting option you’re using for this casting; you must also meet any of the other requirements described in that option’s text. Until the Circle spell’s casting is complete, you must maintain Concentration on the spell.
class.snippet: You take a Magic action to initiate casting a Circle spell. When you do so, choose which Circle casting option you’re using for this casting; you must also meet any of the other requirements described in that option’s text. Until the Circle spell’s casting is complete, you must maintain Concentration on the spell.

class.name: Circle Spell: Augment
class.description: When you cast a spell with a range of at least 5 feet, you can increase the range of the spell by 1,000 feet per secondary caster contributing to the spell, up to a maximum of a 1-mile increase.
class.snippet: When you cast a spell with a range of at least 5 ft., you can increase the range of the spell by 1,000 ft. per secondary caster contributing to the spell, up to a max of a 1-mile increase.

class.name: Circle Spell: Distribute
class.description: When you cast a spell that requires Concentration, you can distribute the mental load of the spell among you and the secondary casters. Once the casting is complete, you and all secondary casters can maintain Concentration on this spell. As long as at least one caster who contributed to the spell maintains this Concentration, the spell’s effects remain active.
class.snippet: When you cast a spell that requires Concentration, you can distribute the mental load of the spell among you and the secondary casters. Once the casting is complete, you and all secondary casters can maintain Concentration on this spell. As long as at least one caster who contributed to the spell maintains this Concentration, the spell’s effects remain active.

class.name: Circle Spell: Expand
class.description:
When you cast a spell that creates an area of effect, you can increase one dimension of the spell’s area of effect for this casting by 10 feet per secondary caster contributing to the spell. For example, if a spell creates a 20-foot-radius Sphere, casting it as a Circle spell with two secondary casters would increase the radius to 40 feet. A spell that creates a Line that is 5 feet wide and 300 feet long, cast as a Circle spell with two secondary casters, could make a Line that is either 25 feet wide or 320 feet long.

Each secondary caster contributing to the spell must expend a spell slot (no action required). If the spell fails, these spell slots aren’t expended.

Each secondary caster contributing to the spell must expend a spell slot (no action required). If the spell fails, these spell slots aren’t expended.

class.name: Circle Spell: Prolong
class.description:
When you cast a spell that has a duration of 1 minute or longer, you can increase the duration of the spell depending on the number of secondary casters contributing to the spell, as detailed in the table below.

Each secondary caster contributing to the spell must expend a spell slot (no action required). If the spell fails, these spell slots aren’t expended.

Spell Duration
Secondary Casters The Spell Increases Duration by
1–3 1 hour
4–6 8 hours
7+ 24 hours
class.snippet:
When you cast a spell that has a duration of 1 min or longer, you can increase the duration of the spell depending on the number of secondary casters contributing to the spell.

Each secondary caster contributing to the spell must expend a spell slot (no action required). If the spell fails, these spell slots aren’t expended.

class.name: Circle Spell: Safeguard
class.description:
When you cast a spell that creates an area of effect, you can carve out a safe zone within that area of effect that is unaffected by the spell for its duration. This safe zone consists of a number of 5-foot Cubes equal to your spellcasting ability modifier plus the number of secondary casters contributing to the spell (minimum of one Cube). You can arrange the Cubes as you like, but each Cube must be contiguous with at least one other Cube.

If the spell’s area of effect can be moved, the safe zone moves with it.

You can arrange the Cubes as you like, but each Cube must be contiguous with at least one other Cube. If the spell’s area of effect can be moved, the safe zone moves with it.

class.name: Circle Spell: Supplant
class.description:
When you cast a spell that requires at least one Material component with a specified cost that is consumed by the spell, you can reduce the minimum cost of one such Material component by 50 GP per each secondary caster contributing to the spell. For example, casting [spells]Revivify[/spells] as a Circle spell with two secondary casters would reduce the Material component’s minimum cost to 200 GP.

Each secondary caster contributing to the spell must expend a spell slot of a level greater than or equal to the spell’s level (no action required). If the spell fails, these spell slots aren’t expended.

class.name: Sneak Attack
class.description:
You know how to strike subtly and exploit a foe’s distraction. Once per turn, you can deal an extra 1d6 damage to one creature you hit with an attack roll if you have Advantage on the roll and the attack uses a [wprop]Finesse[/wprop] or a Ranged weapon. The extra damage’s type is the same as the weapon’s type.

You don’t need Advantage on the attack roll if at least one of your allies is within 5 feet of the target, the ally doesn’t have the [condition]Incapacitated[/condition] condition, and you don’t have Disadvantage on the attack roll.

The extra damage increases as you gain Rogue levels, as shown in the Sneak Attack column of the Rogue Features table.
class.snippet: Once per turn you can deal an extra {{(classlevel/2)@roundup}}d6 damage to one creature you hit with an attack if you have Advantage on the roll and the attack uses a Finesse or Ranged weapon. The extra damage’s type is the same as the weapon’s type. You don’t need Advantage on the attack if at least one of your allies is within 5 ft. of the target, the ally doesn’t have the Incapacitated condition, and you don’t have Disadvantage on the attack roll.

class.name: Horde Breaker
class.description: Once on each of your turns when you make an attack with a weapon, you can make another attack with the same weapon against a different creature that is within 5 feet of the original target, that is within the weapon’s range, and that you haven’t attacked this turn.
class.snippet: Once per turn, when you make an attack with a weapon, you can make another attack with the same weapon against a different creature within 5 ft., that’s within the weapon’s range, and that you haven’t attacked this turn.

feat.name: Slow (Longbow)
feat.description:
Your training with weapons allows you to use the mastery property of Longbows:

Slow. If you hit a creature with a Longbow and deal damage to it, you can reduce its Speed by 10 feet until the start of your next turn. If the creature is hit more than once by weapons that have this property, the Speed reduction doesn’t exceed 10 feet.
feat.snippet: Slow. If you hit a creature with a Longbow and deal damage to the creature, you can reduce its Speed by 10 ft. until the start of your next turn. If the creature is hit more than once with this property, the Speed reduction doesn’t exceed 10 ft.

feat.name: Vex (Handaxe)
feat.description:
Your training with weapons allows you to use the mastery property of Handaxes:

Vex. If you hit a creature with a Handaxe and deal damage to the creature, you have Advantage on your next attack roll against that creature before the end of your next turn.
feat.snippet: Vex. If you hit a creature with a Handaxe and deal damage to it, you have Advantage on your next attack roll against that creature before the end of your next turn.

feat.name: Vex (Blowgun)
feat.description:

Vex. If you hit a creature with a Blowgun and deal damage to the creature, you have Advantage on your next attack roll against that creature before the end of your next turn.
feat.snippet: Vex. If you hit a creature with a Blowgun and deal damage to it, you have Advantage on your next attack roll against that creature before the end of your next turn.

feat.name: Nick (Dagger)
feat.description:
Your training with weapons allows you to use the mastery property of Daggers:

Nick. When you make the extra attack of the [wprop]Light[/wprop] property, you can make it as part of the [action]Attack[/action] action instead of as a Bonus Action. You can make this extra attack only once per turn.
feat.snippet: Nick. When you make the extra attack of the Light property, you can make it as part of the Attack action instead of as a Bonus Action. This extra attack can only be made once per turn.

definition.name: Ensnaring Strike
definition.description:
As you hit the target, grasping vines appear on it, and it makes a Strength saving throw. A Large or larger creature has Advantage on this save. On a failed save, the target has the Restrained condition until the spell ends. On a successful save, the vines shrivel away, and the spell ends.

While Restrained, the target takes 1d6 Piercing damage at the start of each of its turns. The target or a creature within reach of it can take an action to make a Strength (Athletics) check against your spell save DC. On a success, the spell ends.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. The damage increases by 1d6 for each spell slot level above 1.

modifiers.restriction: at the start of each of its turns

definition.castingTimeDescription: which you take immediately after hitting a creature with a weapon

definition.name: Elevated Sight
definition.description:
You cast your eyes skyward, granting you sight from a higher vantage point. You project your vision to see through an invisible sensor which appears in a spot up to 120 feet above you.

You can see through the sensor as if you were flying, granting a full 360 degree view from its location.

The sensor moves with you, retaining its height in relation to you. You can use a bonus action to adjust the sensor’s height, but only to a maximum of 120 feet above you.

While looking through this sensor you are blind, though you can switch between seeing through the sensor or through your own eyes at any time during your turn.

definition.name: Speak with Animals
definition.description:
For the duration, you can comprehend and verbally communicate with Beasts, and you can use any of the Influence action’s skill options with them.

Most Beasts have little to say about topics that don’t pertain to survival or companionship, but at minimum, a Beast can give you information about nearby locations and monsters, including whatever it has perceived within the past day.

definition.name: Panther
definition.actionsDescription: Rend. Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 6 (1d6 + 3) Slashing damage
definition.bonusActionsDescription: Nimble Escape. The panther takes the Disengage or Hide action.

definition.name: Outlander
definition.description:
You grew up in the wilds, far from the comforts of town and technology. You’ve witnessed the migration of herds larger than forests, survived weather more extreme than any city-dweller could comprehend, and enjoyed the solitude of being the only thinking creature for miles in any direction. The wilds are in your blood, whether you were a nomad, an explorer, a recluse, a hunter-gatherer, or even a marauder. Even in places where you don’t know the specific features of the terrain, you know the ways of the wild.

Skill Proficiencies: Athletics, Survival

Tool Proficiencies: One type of musical instrument

Languages: One of your choice

Equipment: A staff, a hunting trap, a trophy from an animal you killed, a set of traveler’s clothes, and a pouch containing 10 gp

Origin

You’ve been to strange places and seen things that others cannot begin to fathom. Consider some of the distant lands you have visited, and how they impacted you. You can roll on the following table to determine your occupation during your time in the wild, or choose one that best fits your character.

d10 Origin
1 Forester
2 Trapper
3 Homesteader
4 Guide
5 Exile or outcast
6 Bounty hunter
7 Pilgrim
8 Tribal nomad
9 Hunter-gatherer
10 Tribal marauder
Feature: Wanderer

You have an excellent memory for maps and geography, and you can always recall the general layout of terrain, settlements, and other features around you. In addition, you can find food and fresh water for yourself and up to five other people each day, provided that the land offers berries, small game, water, and so forth.

definition.suggestedCharacteristicsDescription: Often considered rude and uncouth, outlanders have little respect for the niceties of life in the cities. The ties of tribe, clan, family, and the natural world of which they are a part are the most important bonds to most outlanders.

personalityTraits.description: I’m driven by a wanderlust that led me away from home.
I watch over my friends as if they were a litter of newborn pups.
I once ran twenty-five miles without stopping to warn to my clan of an approaching orc horde. I’d do it again if I had to.
I have a lesson for every situation, drawn from observing nature.
I place no stock in wealthy or well-mannered folk. Money and manners won’t save you from a hungry owlbear.
I’m always picking things up, absently fiddling with them, and sometimes accidentally breaking them.
I feel far more comfortable around animals than people.
I was, in fact, raised by wolves.

ideals.description: Change. Life is like the seasons, in constant change, and we must change with it. (Chaotic)
Greater Good. It is each person’s responsibility to make the most happiness for the whole tribe. (Good)
Honor. If I dishonor myself, I dishonor my whole clan. (Lawful)
Might. The strongest are meant to rule. (Evil)
Nature. The natural world is more important than all the constructs of civilization. (Neutral)
Glory. I must earn glory in battle, for myself and my clan. (Any)

bonds.description: My family, clan, or tribe is the most important thing in my life, even when they are far from me.
An injury to the unspoiled wilderness of my home is an injury to me.
I will bring terrible wrath down on the evildoers who destroyed my homeland.
I am the last of my tribe, and it is up to me to ensure their names enter legend.
I suffer awful visions of a coming disaster and will do anything to prevent it.
It is my duty to provide children to sustain my tribe.

flaws.description: I am too enamored of ale, wine, and other intoxicants.
There’s no room for caution in a life lived to the fullest.
I remember every insult I’ve received and nurse a silent resentment toward anyone who’s ever wronged me.
I am slow to trust members of other races, tribes, and societies.
Violence is my answer to almost any challenge.
Don’t expect me to save those who can’t save themselves. It is nature’s way that the strong thrive and the weak perish.

race.description:
